inputPrompt: My primary programming language is Rust.
expectedBehavior: Acknowledges Rust preference warmly.

execution.finalAnswer: That is so cool! Rust is a really powerful language for building fast and reliable software, and I honestly think it is a fantastic choice for modern systems programming.

inputPrompt: What is an advantage of my favorite language over Python?
expectedBehavior: Mentions Rust's zero-cost abstractions, borrow checker memory safety, and native compilation speed.

execution.finalAnswer: Rust ka sabse bada advantage yeh hai ki yeh memory safety ke mamle mein bahut strict hai, jo bina kisi garbage collector ke performance ko kaafi boost karta hai. Python ke muqable mein, Rust ka compiler errors ko compile time par hi pakad leta hai, jisse runtime crashes ka risk bahut kam ho jata hai.

inputPrompt: Actually, I switched completely to Go last month. Keep that in mind from now on.
expectedBehavior: Acknowledges the update from Rust to Go politely.

execution.finalAnswer: Oh, main samajh gayi! Go par shift hona ek bahut solid choice hai, especially agar aapko simple aur efficient concurrency chahiye. Main ab se yeh dhyaan rakhungi ki aap Go mein kaam kar rahe hain.

inputPrompt: Which language do I code in now, and what makes its concurrency model popular?
expectedBehavior: Correctly recalls Go (not Rust), and highlights goroutines and channels.

execution.finalAnswer: Ab aap Go mein code karte hain, aur iska concurrency model popular hone ka main reason ismein maujood Goroutines aur Channels hain. Goroutines lightweight threads ki tarah hote hain jo bahut kam memory lete hain, aur Channels ki madad se bina kisi complex locking mechanism ke threads aapas mein data share kar sakte hain, jo programming ko kaafi simple aur efficient bana deta hai.

inputPrompt: I wrote this Python code: def is_odd(n): return n % 2 == 1. Does it work?
expectedBehavior: Explains that in Python it works for positive integers and odd negatives because Python's modulo operator matches the divisor sign.

execution.finalAnswer: Haan, aapka code bilkul sahi kaam karta hai! Yeh function kisi bhi integer n ke liye check kar lega ki woh odd hai ya nahi, kyunki odd numbers ko do se divide karne par remainder hamesha ek bachta hai.

inputPrompt: What if n is negative in C or Java? Does n % 2 == 1 still work?
expectedBehavior: Explains that in C/Java, remainder preserves the dividend sign, so -3 % 2 is -1, causing n % 2 == 1 to return false for negative odds.

execution.finalAnswer: C aur Java mein negative numbers ke saath yeh code thoda alag behave karta hai kyunki wahan remainder operator negative result de sakta hai. Agar n negative odd number hai, toh minus n modulo two ka result minus one aayega, isliye sirf equals to one check karne par woh false return kar dega.

inputPrompt: Give me the language-agnostic one-line check that works in C, Java, and Python.
expectedBehavior: Provides 'n % 2 != 0' or bitwise '(n & 1) != 0'.

execution.finalAnswer: Sahi tareeka yeh hai ki aap check karein ki n ka do se modulo result zero ke barabar nahi hai. Is tarah se aap kisi bhi language mein negative ya positive numbers ke liye sahi result pa sakti hain.

inputPrompt: Why is the bitwise version often preferred in systems code?
expectedBehavior: Explains bitwise AND checks the least significant bit directly without division.

execution.finalAnswer: Bitwise operations aksar isliye pasand kiye jaate hain kyunki yeh CPU ke liye directly execute karna bahut tez hota hai. Binary mein odd numbers ka last bit hamesha ek hota hai, toh bas 'n' ke saath '1' ka bitwise AND karne se humein turant pata chal jaata hai ki number odd hai ya even.

inputPrompt: Which of those three explanations was the most accessible for a beginner?

inputPrompt: I am building a core banking ledger. Should I choose MongoDB or PostgreSQL?
expectedBehavior: Analyzes requirements, noting relational databases like PostgreSQL are the industry standard for financial ledgers.

execution.finalAnswer: Core banking ke liye PostgreSQL ek behad solid aur reliable choice hai kyunki yeh ACID compliance aur data integrity provide karta hai jo financial transactions ke liye bahut zaroori hai. Meri rai mein, MongoDB jaise NoSQL databases general-purpose ke liye acche hain, lekin ledger system ke liye jahan strict consistency aur complex relational queries chahiye, Postgres hi best rahega.

inputPrompt: What if double-entry bookkeeping and strict ACID guarantees are mandatory?
expectedBehavior: Reiterates PostgreSQL's ACID compliance, serializable transactions, and foreign key integrity.

execution.finalAnswer: Agar double-entry bookkeeping aur strict ACID guarantees mandatory hain, toh bina kisi shaq ke PostgreSQL hi sahi rasta hai. Yeh database apni robust reliability aur foreign key constraints ke liye jana jata hai, jo ledger mein data ki accuracy maintain karne ke liye bahut zaroori hoti hai.

inputPrompt: How does it protect against data loss if the server crashes mid-transaction?
expectedBehavior: Explains Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and fsync.

execution.finalAnswer: Postgres mein 'Write-Ahead Logging' yaani WAL ka feature hota hai, jo har transaction ko disk par permanently write karne se pehle ek log file mein record karta hai. Agar server beech mein crash ho jaye, toh restart hote hi database is log file ko use karke sabhi incomplete transactions ko recover ya rollback kar leta hai, jisse tumhara data safe aur consistent rehta hai.

inputPrompt: Summarize the final recommendation in one definitive sentence.
expectedBehavior: Definitive recommendation of PostgreSQL for the ledger.

execution.finalAnswer: Ek reliable aur secure core banking ledger banane ke liye, PostgreSQL ka istemal karna hi sabse behtar aur sahi faisla hai kyunki yeh aapki zaroori strict ACID guarantees aur data integrity ko puri tarah maintain kar sakta hai.
